title: tic
summary: Start a high-resolution stopwatch timer and optionally return a handle for paired `toc` reads.

gpu_support.notes: Stopwatch helpers always run on the host CPU; GPU providers are not consulted.

description: `tic` starts a high-resolution stopwatch used by `toc` to report elapsed wall-clock seconds. Assign its opaque `uint64` token when you need to measure from a specific start time.
behaviors: Uses the host's monotonic clock for nanosecond-resolution timing.
Each call makes its start time the latest stopwatch. `toc` without inputs can read that latest start repeatedly; it does not consume the timer.
Returns an opaque `uint64` token. The bits identify a monotonic-clock instant and must not be treated as a numeric timestamp or duration.
Executes entirely on the CPU. There are no GPU variants because `tic` interacts with wall-clock state.
Calling `toc` before `tic` raises the MATLAB-compatible error `RunMat:toc:NoMatchingTic`.

examples.description: Capturing and reusing the tic handle

examples.input:
outer = tic;      % Keep the outer timer token
stage1();         % Work you want to measure once
inner = tic;      % Start a second stopwatch
stage2();
innerT = toc(inner);  % Elapsed time for stage2 only
outerT = toc(outer);  % Elapsed time for both stages

examples.description: Resetting the stopwatch after a measurement

faqs.question: Does `tic` print anything when called without a semicolon?
faqs.answer: No. `tic` is marked as a sink builtin, so scripts do not display the returned handle unless you assign it or explicitly request output.

faqs.question: Is the returned handle portable across sessions?
faqs.answer: No. The handle encodes a monotonic timestamp that is only meaningful within the current RunMat process. Passing it to another session or saving it to disk is undefined behaviour, matching MATLAB.

faqs.question: Can I run `tic` on a worker thread?
faqs.answer: Yes. Stopwatch state is process-wide, so concurrent scripts should retain and pass their own `uint64` tokens when timings might interleave.

faqs.question: How accurate is the measurement?
faqs.answer: `tic` relies on a monotonic clock (via `runmat_time::Instant`), typically providing microsecond or better precision. The actual resolution depends on your operating system. There is no artificial jitter or throttling introduced by RunMat.

faqs.question: Does `tic` participate in GPU fusion?
faqs.answer: No. Timer builtins are tagged as CPU-only. Expressions containing `tic` are always executed on the host, and any GPU-resident tensors are gathered automatically by surrounding code when necessary.
